key_insights: The halving event will serve as a market health check to gauge underlying strength or weakness rather than being a major catalyst itself
JP Morgan expects BTC to dip post-halving, which both hosts dismiss as ghost-written with weak arguments about overbought conditions and volatility-adjusted pricing
BTC ETF flows have slowed significantly from the March 12th peak of 1 billion daily inflow, with some outflows and zero-flow days testing institutional patience
The 61-72k BTC range has 'shitty' battered support and resistance, making it difficult to trade either direction
ETH/BTC pair continues to look weak and 'sad' at the lows, though ETH itself bounced from 2900-3k support
WIF remains a hot altcoin that moves more than BTC in both directions due to retail holder base
NFTs like Bored Apes have declined 90% from highs while ETH is only down 30-40%
Bitcoin NFTs and ordinals are seen as the next area for asymmetrical opportunities
summary: Cred and Duck analyze the pre-halving BTC market, which is stuck in a 'shitty' 61-72k range with battered support and resistance. Cred remains cautious, preferring a downside breakout below 60k, while Duck sees potential for upside if 68k breaks targeting 78k. Both are skeptical of the halving as a major catalyst, viewing it more as a health check event to gauge market strength. ETH/BTC looks weak at the lows, though ETH USD bounced from the 2900-3k support level. ETF flows have slowed from March highs, and JP Morgan's bearish post-halving prediction is dismissed as having weak arguments.
